content.text: No liquidated damages, penalties, or Customer-payable termination fees appear anywhere in the document. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: (c) Expenses of Servicing Transition. All reasonable expenses incurred by the Issuer, the Owner Trustee, the Indenture Trustee and the Successor Servicer in connection with (i) the transition of servicing rights and obligations to the Successor Servicer and (ii) amending this Agreement or entering into an assumption agreement or new agreement to reflect a succession of the Servicer will be paid by the resigning or terminated Servicer on receipt of an invoice in reasonable detail.
input.rationale: Searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty", "termination fee", "make-whole" and "forfeit" return no provision imposing liquidated damages or a penalty on the Issuer or Depositor (our parties). This meets the preferred position of no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties, so no redline is warranted. The termination architecture in fact runs in our favour: on Servicer resignation or removal under Article VII there is no break fee, make-whole or minimum-fee payable by the Issuer to Cellco, Cellco must continue performing and assumes the Section 2.5/2.6 and Master Trust receivables-acquisition obligations (p0316, p0327), and Section 7.5(c) makes the resigning or terminated Servicer bear all reasonable transition expenses of the Issuer, the Trustees and the Successor Servicer (p0347). Section 8.3 termination is event-driven with no exit payment. Two items noted but not deviations: (i) the $150,000 appointment fee and Additional Successor Servicer Fee under Section 7.4(c) (p0339) are compensation for services rendered by a third-party replacement servicer paid out of Collections, not a liquidated amount owed to the counterparty; and (ii) Make-Whole Payments under Article VIII are noteholder prepayment economics arising only from a voluntary Optional Redemption elected by the Class A Certificateholder, not a penalty imposed on us by the Servicer/Marketing Agent. Marketing Agent and Servicer deposit/remittance shortfall mechanics in Articles IV and VI likewise impose payment obligations on the counterparty, which benefit our side and are not flagged.
